findings.title: Cleanup job interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The background cleanup ticker was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This is unrelated to the deadlock fix and makes all cleanup jobs (temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) run 10x more often, which increases DB load substantially on large installs. Also, the per-run timeout is 9 minutes, so runs can now overlap/queue behind each other. This looks like a leftover debugging change and should be reverted.

findings.title: Debug logging left in at Error level, dumping all IDs on every batch
findings.body: `r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", ..., "ids", ids, ...)` and the equivalent calls at lines 537, 554, 557, 576 and 579 log normal successful operation at ERROR severity, and include the entire batch of IDs (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, default in the thousands) in each message. This will spam error logs/alerting on every cleanup cycle and produce huge log lines. These should be removed or downgraded to Debug without the full ID slice.

findings.title: Parameter-limit workaround only guards SQLite; other drivers can exceed placeholder limits
findings.body: deleteByIDs inlines IDs only when `GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite && AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`. For Postgres (pq limits a statement to 65535 parameters) and MySQL (max_prepared_stmt / packet limits), a large configured AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize will produce a DELETE with that many placeholders and fail at runtime. Additionally the condition is based on the configured batch size rather than `len(ids)`, so behaviour depends on config rather than the actual statement being built. Consider chunking the ID list to a fixed safe size (e.g. 999) for all dialects.
